items.title: Finite coefficient observation and innovation interface
items.statement:
Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$. For each integer $k$ with $0\le k\le T$, let $V_k$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space with an ordered basis $\Phi_k=(\phi_{k,1},\ldots,\phi_{k,m_k})$, where $m_k\ge1$. An ordered basis is a linearly independent spanning list. A coefficient vector $a_k=(a_{k,1},\ldots,a_{k,m_k})^T\in\mathbb R^{m_k}$ represents the trial field $u_k=\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}a_{k,j}\phi_{k,j}\in V_k$. This is a finite-dimensional representation; it does not assert that a fluid field in an untruncated model belongs to $V_k$.

For each $1\le k\le T$, choose a real linear observation map $L_k:V_k\to\mathbb R^{p_k}$, with $p_k\ge1$, and a real matrix $F_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k\times m_{k-1}}$ for the coefficient transition. The observation matrix $H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times m_k}$ is defined by $[H_k]_{ij}=[L_k(\phi_{k,j})]_i$; hence $L_k(u_k)=H_ka_k$. A symmetric matrix $C$ is positive semidefinite, written $C\succeq0$, when $v^TCv\ge0$ for every vector $v$ of matching dimension, and is positive definite, written $C\succ0$, when this inequality is strict for every nonzero $v$.

For stochastic assimilation, assume the Axiom of Choice (AC), meaning every family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the Gaussian-law construction. Choose an instance of the finite linear-Gaussian state-space model with independent noises: $a_0\sim N_{m_0}(\mu_0,P_0)$, $q_k\sim N_{m_k}(0,Q_k)$, and $r_k\sim N_{p_k}(0,R_k)$ are mutually independent, with $P_0,Q_k,R_k\succeq0$, and
$$a_k=F_ka_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad y_k=H_ka_k+r_k.$$
Here $N_d(\mu,C)$ denotes the $d$-dimensional Gaussian law with mean $\mu$ and symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance $C$, including singular $C$. For a Kalman-filter run, write $m^a_{k-1}$ and $P^a_{k-1}$ for its previous analysis mean and covariance, and define its forecast mean and covariance, innovation, and innovation covariance by
$$m^f_k=F_km^a_{k-1},\qquad P^f_k=F_kP^a_{k-1}F_k^T+Q_k,\qquad d_k=y_k-H_km^f_k,\qquad S_k=H_kP^f_kH_k^T+R_k.$$
The admissible filter inputs are those for which each innovation covariance to be solved is positive definite. The gain is the solution $K_k=P^f_kH_k^TS_k^{-1}$, computed by the supplied Cholesky solves, and the analysis outputs are $m^a_k=m^f_k+K_kd_k$ and $P^a_k=P^f_k-K_kS_kK_k^T$. The formula describes the exact target of the supplied recursion; it is not an instruction to form a matrix inverse numerically.

For a one-step perturbed-observation ensemble Kalman update, choose dimensions $m,p\ge1$, a linear observation matrix $H\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}$, a datum $y\in\mathbb R^p$, an ensemble size $N\ge2$, and a positive-definite observation covariance $\Gamma\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$. Given forecast coefficients $\hat a^1,\ldots,\hat a^N\in\mathbb R^m$, take perturbations $\eta^i\sim N_p(0,\Gamma)$ independent across members and independent of the forecast ensemble. Define $\bar a=N^{-1}\sum_i\hat a^i$ and the divisor-$N$ covariance $C_N=N^{-1}\sum_i(\hat a^i-\bar a)(\hat a^i-\bar a)^T$. The gain and perturbed-data update are $K_N=C_NH^T(HC_NH^T+\Gamma)^{-1}$ and $a^{a,i}=\hat a^i+K_N(y+\eta^i-H\hat a^i)$. Since $C_N\succeq0$, $HC_NH^T+\Gamma\succ0$. This is the specified finite-ensemble procedure; the definition alone gives no finite-ensemble posterior-exactness claim.

In a single-window finite inverse view, a real matrix $G\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}$ maps coefficients $a\in\mathbb R^m$ to predicted observations $Ga$. A datum has the form $y=Ga+e$, where $e\in\mathbb R^p$ is its realized error and a symmetric positive-definite matrix $R\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ is the declared error covariance and weighting matrix. This deterministic inverse interface does not assume a probability distribution for the realized vector $e$.

Choosing a finite trial space, a linearization, or process-noise covariances is part of adopting the finite model. These choices do not show that a nonlinear fluid equation or an actual sensor is described exactly by that model.

items.title: Exact filtering for the declared linear Gaussian model
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $T\ge0$ be finite and take an admissible stochastic coefficient model from the definition of the finite coefficient observation and innovation interface. Thus the coefficient states and observations satisfy $a_k=F_ka_{k-1}+q_k$ and $y_k=H_ka_k+r_k$, the initial state and all process and measurement noises are mutually independent Gaussian vectors with positive-semidefinite covariances, and every innovation covariance $S_k=H_kP^f_kH_k^T+R_k$ used by the recursion is positive definite. Run the finite-horizon Kalman recursion from the declared initial mean and covariance. Then, for each $0\le k\le T$, its Gaussian output is an everywhere-defined conditional-law version for the coefficient state $a_k$ given the observation history $y_{1:k}$. The output mean and covariance are the exact conditional mean and covariance of this declared finite linear-Gaussian model, including at histories that have probability zero under a nonsingular observation law. Initial, process, measurement, forecast-state, and analysis-state covariances may be singular; only the innovation covariances being solved must be positive definite. This is a deduction about the declared finite model, not a claim that a nonlinear or untruncated fluid equation is itself linear-Gaussian.

items.title: EnKF large-ensemble scope and nonlinear limits
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC), meaning every family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the Gaussian-law construction. Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive integers $m_k$ for $0\le k\le T$ and $p_k$ for $1\le k\le T$, matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k\times m_{k-1}}$ and $H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times m_k}$ for $1\le k\le T$, and a finite linear-Gaussian coefficient model
$$a_k=F_ka_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad y_k=H_ka_k+r_k,$$
where $\mu_0\in\mathbb R^{m_0}$, $a_0\sim N_{m_0}(\mu_0,P_0)$, $q_k\sim N_{m_k}(0,Q_k)$, and $r_k\sim N_{p_k}(0,R_k)$ are mutually independent, $P_0,Q_k$ are positive semidefinite, and $R_k$ is positive definite. Fix arbitrary observation data $y_{1:T}$. For each ensemble size $N\ge2$, draw the initial members $a_{N,i}^{a,0}$ independently from $N_{m_0}(\mu_0,P_0)$. At each $k$, draw process perturbations $q_{N,i}^k\sim N_{m_k}(0,Q_k)$ and observation perturbations $\eta_{N,i}^k\sim N_{p_k}(0,R_k)$, with all these perturbations mutually independent across members and times and independent of the initial ensemble, and set $a_{N,i}^{f,k}=F_ka_{N,i}^{a,k-1}+q_{N,i}^k$. Define $\bar a_N^{f,k}=N^{-1}\sum_i a_{N,i}^{f,k}$ and the divisor-$N$ covariance $C_N^{f,k}=N^{-1}\sum_i(a_{N,i}^{f,k}-\bar a_N^{f,k})(a_{N,i}^{f,k}-\bar a_N^{f,k})^T$. The common gain and perturbed-observation update are
$$K_N^k=C_N^{f,k}H_k^T(H_kC_N^{f,k}H_k^T+R_k)^{-1},\qquad a_{N,i}^{a,k}=a_{N,i}^{f,k}+K_N^k(y_k+\eta_{N,i}^k-H_ka_{N,i}^{f,k}).$$
Since $C_N^{f,k}$ is positive semidefinite and $R_k$ is positive definite, this inverse exists. Define the analysis empirical mean and covariance by $\bar a_N^{a,k}=N^{-1}\sum_i a_{N,i}^{a,k}$ and $C_N^{a,k}=N^{-1}\sum_i(a_{N,i}^{a,k}-\bar a_N^{a,k})(a_{N,i}^{a,k}-\bar a_N^{a,k})^T$. Let $m_{k|k}$ and $P_{k|k}$ be the mean and covariance produced by the exact Kalman recursion in the preceding filtering proposition, which defines an everywhere-defined Gaussian filtering law at every fixed history $y_{1:k}$. At each fixed $k\le T$, $\bar a_N^{a,k}$ and $C_N^{a,k}$ converge in probability to $m_{k|k}$ and $P_{k|k}$ as $N\to\infty$; moreover, for each fixed bounded Lipschitz function $\varphi:\mathbb R^{m_k}\to\mathbb R$, $N^{-1}\sum_i\varphi(a_{N,i}^{a,k})$ converges in probability to its integral under that filtering law. Here bounded Lipschitz means $\sup_x|\varphi(x)|<\infty$ and $|\varphi(x)-\varphi(x')|\le L\|x-x'\|_2$ for some finite $L$ and all $x,x'$. Convergence in probability means that for every $\epsilon>0$, the probability that the error exceeds $\epsilon$ tends to zero; use Euclidean norm for vectors, Frobenius norm for matrices, and absolute value for scalars. All probabilities refer to the ensemble sampling just described. The horizon is fixed as $N$ grows, with no uniform-in-time conclusion. At finite $N$, the common sample-covariance gain couples the update, and the theorem does not assert independent posterior samples or an exact posterior law for the ensemble. It covers the stated linear maps and perturbed-observation formula only. Covariance localization here means replacing the sample covariance by its entrywise product with a prescribed taper matrix; covariance inflation means rescaling the ensemble anomalies by a factor greater than one or adding a prescribed positive-semidefinite covariance; a transport update means applying a selected map to ensemble members instead of the displayed perturbed-observation formula. These modified procedures and nonlinear state or observation maps require their own statements and proofs. The claim is conditional on the chosen finite model; it is not a conclusion that a nonlinear fluid equation or an actual flow is described by it.

items.title: Whitened observation identifiability and stability
items.statement:
Let $E$ be a nonzero linear subspace of the finite coefficient space $\mathbb R^m$, let $G:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^p$ be the declared linear observation map, and let $R\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be symmetric positive definite. Let $R^{1/2}$ be the unique symmetric positive-semidefinite square root of $R$ and set $W=(R^{1/2})^{-1}$, so $W^TW=R^{-1}$. The whitened map is $A=W(G|_E):E\to\mathbb R^p$, and define its smallest gain by $\sigma_{\min}(A)=\inf\{\|Av\|_2:v\in E,\ \|v\|_2=1\}$; the singular-value decomposition shows this infimum is the smallest singular value and is attained. Identifiability on $E$ means injectivity of $G|_E$. It holds exactly when $\sigma_{\min}(A)>0$. If it holds, then for every true $a\in E$, every realized error $e\in\mathbb R^p$, and datum $y=Ga+e$, the unique weighted least-squares estimate $\hat a=\arg\min_{b\in E}\|W(y-Gb)\|_2$ satisfies
$$\|\hat a-a\|_2\le\frac{\|We\|_2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}.$$
If $\sigma_{\min}(A)=0$, a nonzero vector in $E\cap\ker G$ makes distinct coefficients observationally indistinguishable. The estimate is pointwise in the realized error; it is not a confidence or probability statement. If a pressure representation includes an additive-constant coefficient direction in $\ker G$, that direction must be fixed or quotiented out to obtain identifiable coefficients. This finite-dimensional result is not a general coefficient-identifiability theorem for a partial differential equation.

title: Assimilation and finite inverse identifiability — Examples

items.title: One sensor cannot identify two independent coefficients
items.statement: Let $V=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_1,\phi_2\}$ have the ordered basis $(\phi_1,\phi_2)$, and represent a candidate field by the coefficient vector $a=(a_1,a_2)^T\in\mathbb R^2$. A single sensor has the linear observation matrix $G=[1\ 0]\in\mathbb R^{1\times2}$, the weighting covariance is $R=[1]$, and a datum is $y=Ga+e$ for a fixed realized error $e\in\mathbb R$. The sensor depends on $a_1$ alone, so it cannot determine $a_2$ on the full two-dimensional coefficient space.
